resources.string: Bluetooth controller for Windows with touch controls. The volume buttons can work as triggers.
DuckPad needs Bluetooth permission to show up on your PC as a controller.
Ready. Start a session to play.
Session open, waiting for the PC.
The last session was cut off while the PC was connected. If it does not connect when you start, remove DuckPad in Windows and add it again.
The last session ended unexpectedly. Try starting; if the PC cannot restore the controller, remove DuckPad in Windows and pair again.
Session open. Leave the controller with back to end it.
1. Tap Start session on this phone.
2. On the PC, click Connect in the DuckPad notification. If it doesn\'t show up, open Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Add device > Bluetooth.
3. Two entries starting with DuckPad show up. Choose the one with the two-device icon, not the phone. The order in the list may change.
In the Windows list, choose DuckPad with the two-device icon, not the one with the phone icon.
4. When the controller says Connected, play. Next time, just tap Start session: Windows connects by itself. To finish, press back twice or tap End session.
Each orientation saves its own layout. End the session to switch.
Use the volume buttons on the controller
By default, Volume − is LT and Volume + is RT. You can change it below. Outside the controller, volume works as usual.

These are the three numbers Windows uses to recognize the controller, in hexadecimal. Windows stores them when pairing: if you change them, end the session, remove DuckPad in Settings > Bluetooth & devices and pair it again. Without that step, Windows ignores the change or leaves the controller half set up.
The DuckPad identity, 1209:0001, is a shared pid.codes test number: other devices under test may use it too.
Using another manufacturer\'s numbers is your responsibility.
Identity %1$s saved: %2$s. It applies to the next session, after pairing again.
Identity %1$s restored: %2$s. It applies to the next session, after pairing again.
The fields below change the chosen identity. Switching between them also means removing DuckPad in Windows and pairing it again.
Now using identity %1$s (%2$s). It applies to the next session, after removing DuckPad in Windows and pairing it again.
End the session to change the identity.
Waiting for the PC. First time? Add “DuckPad” in its Bluetooth settings
Wrong entry: remove it in Windows and pick the DuckPad without a phone icon
Windows kept an old pairing: remove DuckPad in Windows and add it again
Still waiting for the PC. Check its Bluetooth. If it will not connect, turn Bluetooth off for 10 seconds and back on before trying to pair again.
Windows has not confirmed the controller yet. Still trying to connect. If it will not respond, turn the PC Bluetooth off for 10 seconds and back on.
The app closed abruptly while the PC was connected, and Windows has dropped the controller. Remove DuckPad in Windows and add it again.
this phone can\'t advertise over Bluetooth LE
Press back again to leave the controller
Left stick. To move it, rest a finger on the left half of the screen and drag.
Right stick. To move it, rest a finger on the right half of the screen and drag.
Drag to move. Tap a control, then pinch or use − + to resize
Move toolbar to the other edge
The dead zone ignores small thumb movements. With finer control, small movements turn less and a full push still reaches the edge. A bigger stick in Arrange controls also gives more travel.
